pages.name: A spanner on a nut
pages.text: You have met a force's turning effect, its [[moment]], as F r sin θ. It is the force times its distance from the pivot, measured at right angles to the force's line. On a spanner, the pivot is the middle of the nut. 150 N at 0.3 m gives 150 × 0.3 = 45 N m. Push at half the distance and you get half the turning effect.

pages.name: A slanted pull
pages.task: A 200 N pull acts on the end of a 0.5 m bar. It is slanted, so its line passes 0.3 m from the pivot. What is its moment?
pages.why: A force can slide along its own line without changing its moment. So slide the pull to the point on its line nearest the pivot. There, the distance to the pivot meets the line at right angles. That distance, 0.3 m, is the [[arm]]. It is the bar's 0.5 m times sin θ, where θ is the angle between the bar and the pull. Here sin θ is 0.6. So the moment is 200 × 0.3 = 60 N m.

pages.name: Balance on a plank
pages.text: When something stays still, its turning effects balance. The clockwise moments add up to the same as the anticlockwise moments. That is the [[principle of moments]]. Here 400 N presses 1.5 m left of the pivot. That gives 400 × 1.5 = 600 N m anticlockwise. On the right, 600 N presses 1 m out. That gives 600 × 1 = 600 N m clockwise. So the plank stays level.

pages.name: Balance the plank
pages.task: 300 N presses on a plank 2 m left of its pivot. Where on the right must 600 N press to balance it?
pages.why: 300 N at 2 m gives 300 × 2 = 600 N m anticlockwise. The 600 N load must give 600 N m clockwise. So it must press 600 ÷ 600 = 1 m from the pivot. Twice the load needs half the distance.

pages.text: As the block moves toward a trestle, that trestle's reaction grows and the far one's shrinks. With the block at the middle, each trestle carries half. Here it hangs 3 m along, so the right trestle is nearer and carries more.

pages.name: Which carries more?
pages.task: The 6 kN block hangs 1 m from the left trestle. Which trestle carries more?
pages.why: The block is 1 m from the left trestle and 3 m from the right. Take moments about the block. The left push times 1 m must balance the right push times 3 m. So the left push is three times the right. The nearer trestle, the left one, carries more.

pages.name: An 8 kN block
pages.task: An 8 kN block hangs 3 m from the left trestle. What does the right trestle carry?
pages.why: Take moments about the left trestle. The block gives 8 × 3 = 24 kN m clockwise. The right trestle pushes up 4 m away. So it carries 24 ÷ 4 = 6 kN. The left carries the other 2 kN.

pages.name: The beam's own weight
pages.text: The beam has weight too. Each half of a uniform beam balances the other about its middle. So its whole weight acts there. This beam weighs 2 kN. About the left trestle it adds 2 × 2 = 4 kN m. With the block's 6 kN m, that makes 10 kN m. So the right trestle carries 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 kN. The left carries the rest of the 8 kN, 5.5 kN. A load spread evenly also acts as its total at its middle.

pages.name: A heavier beam
pages.task: A 6 m beam weighs 3 kN. A 4 kN block hangs 1.5 m from the left trestle. What does the right trestle carry?
pages.why: About the left trestle, the block gives 4 × 1.5 = 6 kN m. The beam's 3 kN acts at its middle, 3 m along. It gives 3 × 3 = 9 kN m. That makes 15 kN m. The right trestle pushes up 6 m away, so it carries 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5 kN. The left carries the other 4.5 kN.

pages.name: A couple
pages.text: Two equal pulls in opposite directions, on different lines, add up to no push at all. They only turn. Such a pair is called a [[couple]]. Each hand pulls 100 N on a valve wheel 0.4 m across. About the centre, each gives 100 × 0.2 = 20 N m, so the two give 40 N m. About one hand, the other gives 100 × 0.4, still 40 N m. A couple's moment is the same about any point. The twist a motor puts on its shaft is a couple too.

pages.name: Spread over half
pages.task: A 4 m beam weighs 2 kN. A 4 kN load is spread evenly over its right half. What does the right trestle carry?
pages.why: The spread load's total acts at the middle of the right half, 3 m along. About the left trestle it gives 4 × 3 = 12 kN m. The beam's 2 kN at its middle gives 2 × 2 = 4 kN m. That makes 16 kN m. So the right trestle carries 16 ÷ 4 = 4 kN. The left carries the other 2 kN.

pages.name: The centre of gravity
pages.task: A 4 kN pump sits on one end of a 3 m skid and a 2 kN motor on the other. Ignore the skid's own weight. Their [[centre of gravity]] is where their whole weight acts. How far from the pump is it?
pages.why: It is where one support could hold them level. Take moments about the pump. The motor gives 2 × 3 = 6 kN m. Their 6 kN total must give the same. So it acts 6 ÷ 6 = 1 m from the pump. Before a lift, the hook goes over that point.
